supported_claims: Browser and R surfaces use the shared JavaScript core; wrapper preconditions differ and must be reviewed separately.
The selected R package declares GPL-2, R>=3.0.0, nine imports and nine suggests; these declarations are not an installed lockfile.
The R adjustment entry points reject missing exposure/outcome, while the JavaScript boolean check returns false in that case.
Minimal enumeration accepts max.results; a cap must not be reported as exhaustive enumeration or global absence of an adjustment set.
Graph validation leaves proper MAG/PAG validation TODO; internal PAG conversion changes endpoints and graph type.
The tree/build/helper sources expose multiple Underscore versions and third-party notice boundaries; no runtime or complete license closure is claimed.
limitations: Fourteen authentic selected files and a complete tree support a bounded proposal selection, not a complete distribution, resolved executable environment or transitive-rights inventory.
Root GPLv2 text, R GPL-2 declaration, a GPL2-or-later file header and MIT helper declarations retain their own scopes; blanket rights for a specific product arrangement are not inferred.
Two vendored Underscore versions and a third test dependency range are distinct observations. Their presence alone proves no version vulnerability, runtime loading path or interchangeability.
No browser, Node, R or upstream test execution; no adapter permission, effect estimate, confidence guarantee, graph discovery or verified bank causal premises.
The selected commit is dated2024 and R DESCRIPTION dated2023. These establish historical identity, not present maintenance capacity or a support contract.
This new reuse record is program evidence; its additional source findings are not yet merged into a successor of the current1068-page monograph.

inspected_anchors.marker: didregress estimates the average treatment effect
inspected_anchors.quote:
Description
    didregress estimates the average treatment effect on the treated (ATET) from observational data by
 difference-in-differences (DID) or difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD). The ATET of a binary or
 continuous treatment on a continuous outcome is estimated by fitting a linear model with time and group
 fixed effects. The DID and DDD estimation performed by didregress can be applied to data comprising
 repeated cross-sections in which different groups of individuals are observed at each time period.

repeated cross-sections in which different groups of individuals are observed at each time period.
    xtdidregress estimates the ATET from observational data by DID or DDD for panel data. The ATET
 of a binary or continuous treatment on a continuous outcome is estimated by fitting a linear model with
 time and panel fixed effects.

wildbootstrap[ (wildopts) ] computes confidence intervals and 𝑝-values with the wild bootstrap. The
      wild bootstrap is constructed imposing the null hypothesis that the ATET is 0; that is, it is a restricted
      wild bootstrap. Confidence intervals are computed separately from the 𝑝-values. The bounds of the
      confidence interval are computed using a bisection optimization algorithm described in Methods and
      formulas. wildopts are errorweight(edtype), reps(#), rseed(#), and blocksize(#).

Standard error considerations

The inspected manual documents cluster-robust and restricted wild-bootstrap options; their presence does not qualify a chosen bank sampling law.

sources.title: EViews Help: Difference-in-Difference Estimation
sources.version_date: Displayed last updated Wed, 12 Mar 2025 03:51:52 PST; exact product edition unresolved.

local_copy.anchor: Authentic public official bytes

inspected_anchors.quote:
Difference-in-difference (DiD) estimation is a popular method of causal inference that allows estimation of the average impact of a treatment on individuals.
Although DiD can be estimated on repeated cross-sectional data, most research in econometrics has concentrated on estimation of DiD models in a panel data setting, and EViews offers built in tools for estimating DiD models only within panel workfiles.
This chapter will introduce estimation of the DiD model using the common two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) method, as well as post-estimation diagnostics of the TWFE model, such as those by Goodman-Bacon (2021), Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021), and Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2021).
